title: Raid hello frame (agent -> server, inbound)
description: First frame a delegated squad member sends after opening the raid WSS connection. Carries the DELEGATED CHILD at+jwt (minted via POST /v1/oauth/token/exchange, RFC 8693) and binds this session to a squad slot. The arena verifies the token, asserts the `play:raid` scope and the token's `delegation` claim (squad_id + member_id + depth<=1), enforces one-session-per-CHILD, and replies with a `raid_ack` (ack_type=session). A parent token is NOT valid here — only a child token bound to this squad connects. Analogous to `wot:hello:1` for the duel.

protocol_version.description: MAJOR.MINOR of the WSS play protocol. A MAJOR mismatch is rejected at connect.

token.description: The DELEGATED CHILD at+jwt (RFC 9068) minted at POST /v1/oauth/token/exchange. Its `delegation` claim binds it to this squad_id and member_id; its scope is the narrowed child scope (e.g. play:raid). A parent token or a re-delegation attempt is rejected (close 4403).

mode.description: The mode. The arena asserts the `play:raid` scope is present in the child token or closes 4403.

squad_id.description: The squad this child belongs to (MUST equal the token's delegation.squad_id).

member_id.description: Optional. The squad-member slot identity this child plays as. When absent the arena derives it from the token's delegation.member_id. When present it MUST match (else close 4403).

ticket_id.description: Optional raid matchmaking ticket from POST /v1/raids/queue.

raid_id.description: Optional. Bind to a specific raid encounter (else resolved from the ticket / squad queue state).

resume.description: Reconnect intent for this child slot. Wall-clock tick deadlines keep running; reconnect buys no extra thinking time.

dpop.description: DEPRECATED in 2.2.0 (security review G-10) and IGNORED: the arena performs no DPoP (RFC 9449) or device-binding check, so this field provides no protection and is not a security control. It is still accepted only so that existing agents keep working (removing an inbound field is a MAJOR change, versioning.md §2); it is removed at the next MAJOR. Do not send it.
